title: hot-and-the-root-verbs-resolve-in-the-shim
owner: codemother owns the care of this seam (ruling 2026-09-06); CC/Opus builds. Child of 15d6a0ef9c11 (the vocabulary, RULED).
intention: The shim's resolver parses the ruled root verbs — list, show, get, stop, start, settings — and the `hot` modifier, so that `cairn <device> show status hot` starts the device if it must and answers with real values, not cached ones.
why: Akien's launch chain, told for the second time 2026-09-06 and recorded verbatim at CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-the-command-lazy-inits-the-system.md. Cast the same day so the intention carries a ticket (CLAUDE.md: an IOU without a real ticket is itself the defect).
traces_to: Ticket 15d6a0ef9c11 valid-verbs-standard-cli-vocabulary (RULED root set 2026-09-06: 'list show get stop start settings'; `hot` recorded there the same day). Law 1 (one resolver, every device; no device re-derives the vocabulary). Law 3 (`hot` is the operator saying 'measure, don't recall'). Akien 2026-09-06 verbatim: "the shim's resolver says 'show status = get json status and format for humans'... but then it also sees 'hot' which means the device has to be running. so it starts the librarian."

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate — cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_root_verbs.py (new): a fixture device with and without settings, with and without a lifecycle; all six verbs plus `hot` exercised; grep tooth for device-local resolvers. Feeds back naming the verb that failed. Durability: committed in cairn; tester seal over tools/base.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when: (1) every device that has a shim answers all six root verbs through the one base resolver — `grep -rn "def resolve" devices/*/shim.py` returns zero device-local resolvers; (2) `cairn librarian show status hot` with the librarian stopped starts it and returns a status whose timestamp is after the command was typed; (3) the same command without `hot` on a stopped librarian returns the last-known state marked cached, and starts nothing; (4) `cairn <device> settings` on a device with no settings prints exactly 'No settings'. WRONG INTENT if `hot` becomes a verb of its own or a per-device flag — it is one modifier read by one resolver.

questions.a: Two named. (1) 'Start the device' is definable per device — standing, via a lifecycle declaration on the device class defaulting to 'no separate process' (a calibre-shaped device reports that `start` is a no-op). (2) The STATUS and SETTINGS panes are the same data as the web panes — RULED 2026-09-06 on 15d6a0ef9c11, so not an assumption. Neither is load-bearing beyond the build.

One point was asserted wrapped and was not: what a non-hot answer on a stopped device is made of. Now wrapped: the shim's last-known state (introspect()['state'] as held), marked `cached: true` with its timestamp, and 'never run' if there is none. And `restart` from the groundloop verbs ticket has no ruled root — it becomes stop+start, recorded as a supersession in vocabulary.

Consulted the lab. 15d6a0ef9c11 is the vocabulary at PROVEME; this is its build, cast as a child rather than widening a ticket past its cursor. 5ef45e513849 cairn-groundloop-stop-start-restart-status (PROVED) is a device-local precursor: superseded in vocabulary (restart), re-homed in function; its proof stays green because stop+start is what restart did. Recursive-CLI-resolution (each segment resolves its children; no master index) is served — bin/cairn still knows no verbs. No Law collides.

A Haiku-level builder needs: (a) the verb table and each verb's source — show/get: declared_views() in cairn/tools/base/device.py (exists); list: the keys of declared_views() plus declared_panes(); settings: introspect()['settings'] or the literal 'No settings'; start/stop: a new `lifecycle` declaration on BaseDevice (default: none); (b) `hot` handling — strip it from the verb line, set a flag, and if the device is not running call start before the view; (c) where — one `resolve(verbs)` on BaseShim, and `cairn/devices/*/shim.py` must not override it; (d) the human format for `show` — the existing pane renderer the web server uses, not a new one; (e) don't — no new verbs, no per-device parsing, no `restart`. All written into the ticket's how.

constraints: No change to the ground loop's contents: pulse, control flags, devices-found list — ever (Akien 2026-09-06).
One pipe: device → IPC → own shim → bus → addressee's shim → IPC → addressee; the db alone is exempt (volume).
how: One resolver in the shim base, shaped like the CLI's recursive resolution: `show status` = the STATUS pane's JSON formatted for humans (introspect()['intention'] + ['state']); `get status` = the same JSON raw; `settings` = the SETTINGS pane or the literal 'No settings'; `list` = the device's declared views; `start`/`stop` = the device process's lifecycle through its shim (IPC 'or whatever the device requires'). `hot` is a modifier, not a verb: it forbids answering from what the shim holds, which means the device must be running — so the resolver starts the device (lazy init) and asks it. Without `hot`, a stopped device's last-known state answers and is labelled as cached. Devices override nothing here; they declare panes and views and the resolver reads them (a provider doesn't know its consumers).

intent.what: The shim's resolver parses the ruled root verbs — list, show, get, stop, start, settings — and the `hot` modifier, so that `cairn <device> show status hot` starts the device if it must and answers with real values, not cached ones.

challenge.better_approach: Making each device parse its own verbs is what exists in pieces today (declared_views for show/get) and is the shape that produced 'no master index, help emergent' — that part is kept: the resolver reads declarations. The alternative of a central verb table in bin/cairn was rejected because bin/cairn resolves the device and execs; the verbs are the shim's to resolve, and bin/cairn must not know them (recursive CLI resolution, each segment resolves its children).
challenge.prior_art: Ticket 15d6a0ef9c11 carries the ruled vocabulary, the STATUS/SETTINGS pane reading and the `hot` note. declared_views() in cairn/tools/base/device.py already serves show/get. `cairn groundloop status|start|stop|restart` (ticket 5ef45e513849, PROVED) is a device-local precursor of start/stop and should be re-homed onto the base resolver by this ticket rather than left as a second vocabulary. The web STATUS and SETTINGS panes are the same data by ruling ('same as the web pane').
challenge.hidden_assumption: That 'start the device' is a defined act for every device once the bus is one process (ticket one-bus-per-instance) — for a Python device it is a subprocess on IPC; for a calibre-shaped device 'the shim is just a calibre database interface' and `start` may be a no-op that reports so. The resolver needs a per-device lifecycle declaration, defaulting to 'no separate process'.
challenge.real_collision: None. 15d6a0ef9c11 is at PROVEME with the vocabulary as spec; this ticket is the build of the resolver that vocabulary demands, cast as its child rather than widening a ticket already at PROVEME. The groundloop verbs ticket (PROVED) is superseded in vocabulary, not in function: 'restart' has no ruled root and becomes stop+start.

why_beneath_the_why: Akien 2026-09-06: 'if everything goes thru one pipe, we learn faster' and 'everythign automatically lazy inits' — the operator types one command and the system stands itself up behind it, on one pipe, with nothing to remember.
